title: CUDA Agent: Large-Scale Agentic RL for High-Performance CUDA Kernel Generation
data_curation: A scalable three-stage pipeline produces CUDA-Agent-Ops-6K (6,000 samples, released on HuggingFace). (1) Seed crawling mines reference operators implemented as torch.nn.Module classes from the torch and transformers libraries. (2) Combinatorial synthesis uses an LLM to sample at most 5 torch operator classes and stack them into fused multi-operator tasks; fusion reshapes the optimization landscape by avoiding intermediate global-memory materialization and coupling stages through shared register/SMEM constraints. transformers operators are used only as standalone modules. (3) Rubric filtering keeps only operators executable in both Eager and Compile modes, deterministic, non-constant across inputs (anti-hacking), and with eager runtime in 1-100ms. Decontamination uses an AST-based similarity tool (PythonASTSimilarity) to drop any sample exceeding 0.9 max similarity to KernelBench. Final composition: 83.77% are 2-op compositions; the rest span 1-5 ops plus 1.18% transformers operators.
curriculum: A multi-stage pipeline warms up both actor and critic before agentic RL, motivated by severe domain mismatch (CUDA is <0.01% of pretraining) that made naive RL collapse at 17 steps. Stage 1: single-turn PPO warm-up on the base model (32k context), which serves as both policy and value network. Stage 2 (Actor init): collect agent trajectories from the warmed model, rejection-filter on positive reward (R>0) and clean tool-call patterns, then SFT the actor. Stage 3 (Critic init): Value Pretraining - fit the critic by MSE on GAE targets (gamma=1, lambda=0.95) over sampled trajectories. Stage 4: agentic PPO with 128k context, up to 150 turns training (200 at eval), 150 steps, global batch 1024, actor lr 3e-6, critic lr 6e-6. This ordering yields stable 200-step training with consistent reward growth.
method: CUDA Agent is a large-scale agentic-RL system for CUDA kernel generation built on Seed1.6 (MoE, 23B active / 230B total). The agent loop is ReAct-style, aligned with OpenHands, exposing Bash/Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep tools plus a CUDA SKILL.md (Anthropic Agent Skills paradigm) prescribing a profile->implement->compile/verify->iterate workflow targeting at least 5% speedup over torch.compile. Reward is a discrete robust schedule r in {-1,1,2,3}: -1 on correctness failure, 3 if >5% faster than both eager and compile, 2 if faster than eager only, 1 otherwise, avoiding the outlier/easy-kernel bias of raw speedup. Reward hacking is blocked by permission-protecting eval scripts, forbidding torch.nn.functional fallbacks via context managers, validating on 5 random inputs, careful profiling with sync/warmup/averaging, and disabling web access. PPO uses asymmetric clipping (eps_lower=0.2, eps_higher=0.28, from DAPO). A CPU-GPU decoupled sandbox (Docker terminal + 128 NVIDIA H20 GPU pool) gives process-isolated, noise-free latency measurement.
eval_metrics: Evaluation is on KernelBench Levels 1-3 (250 tasks: L1=100, L2=100, L3=50), adapted to the multi-file dev environment. Three metrics: Pass Rate (compiles and passes correctness), Faster Rate (% correct kernels beating baseline, reported vs both Eager and Compile), and Speed-up (geometric-mean ratio over correct solutions; best trajectory solution per task). Baselines (all under the same agent loop): Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, GLM 4.6, Kimi K2, and Seed1.6 base; ChatGPT-5 models declined CUDA prompts. Headline: CUDA Agent reaches 98.8% pass, 96.8% faster-vs-compile, 2.11x geomean vs compile overall, with 100%/100%/92% faster-vs-compile on L1/L2/L3, beating Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro by about 40% on L3. Ablations isolate gains from the agent loop, robust reward, RFT, and value pretraining. Case studies show up to 73.31x (diagonal matmul) vs torch.compile.
key_results: CUDA Agent (Seed1.6) on KernelBench: 98.8% pass rate, 96.8% faster rate vs torch.compile, 2.11x geomean speedup vs compile overall; 100%/100%/92% faster rate on Level-1/2/3. It outperforms Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro by ~40% on the hardest Level-3 split. Multi-stage warm-up enables stable PPO training for 150 steps versus collapse at 17 steps without it.
evolution_note: CUDA Agent extends the agentic-RL-for-coding line (Kevin's multi-turn RL) by combining DAPO-style asymmetric PPO clipping, ReAct/OpenHands agent loops, and Anthropic's Agent Skills paradigm, while explicitly reacting to training-free CUDA systems (STARK, CudaForge) and data-leakage-prone fine-tuners (CUDA-L1, Kevin). In the 2026 context, it shows that large-scale execution-rewarded agentic RL can make LLMs match or beat compiler-based optimization (torch.compile), motivating automation of performance-critical systems software.
